author: Raiyan Khan ARK
title: This is home.
content:
Playing Clash of Clans since 2015. This is my childhood game. I used to play every single day until around 2018, then life and other games (PUBG Mobile) took over. After that I only opened it now and then — ten or fifteen minutes, a couple times a week, sometimes not at all.
A few years later I installed it again. Within a month I was back on a regular schedule. I even bought scenery and hero skins. I never spent money on Clash of Clans before. I had spent a little on Clash Royale years ago, but this village was always free for me. This time it felt right. Even if I stop playing tomorrow, or uninstall it again after five or ten years, I already know I’ll come back to it someday. That’s what this game is.
I still have my old clan. I was the leader. The last war was in 2018. Everyone is gone and the clan is dead, but I never deleted it. Opening that clan tag still hits different.
Five stars. I’m a 2015 player and this game still has my heart.
One honest request: please keep pushing the graphics. The village, attacks, and older assets still look dated next to the newer skins and sceneries. And please keep adding more quality skins — not just seasonal collabs, but skins that make the heroes and the home village feel fresh for long-time players like us. The cosmetics I bought were worth it. Give us more of that level.
Thank you, Supercell. This game raised a lot of us.

author: RiggedEngine
title: A Rigged Engine That Puts a Thumb on the Scale
content:
I cannot recommend this game to anyone looking for a fair, skill-based competitive experience. Once you spend months or years maxing out your account to reach the top tier, the game completely abandons organic matchmaking. Instead, the backend architecture utilizes an active engagement algorithm to force you into a pre-determined bracket.

The system openly cheats to control your win/loss ratio. If you have a highly successful offensive run, the game will literally manipulate your base visibility to hold back your defensive cycle. The absolute second you log off, the invisible hand drops hyper-optimized, maxed-out meta opponents on your base to wipe out your progress and artificially suppress your leaderboard position.

You are no longer playing against other players; you are fighting a crooked casino engine designed to manage your frustration levels. It completely strips away player agency and destroys the integrity of end-game competition. Do not waste your time reaching the top just to let an algorithm decide when you are allowed to win or lose.

author: hahduudjjebrbx
title: Heros
content: Clash of clans is a classic, and a great game but… the system for upgrading heros is bafflingly terrible. To keep up with upgrading heros, it is extremely expensive. At town hall 15, after completing almost an hour of play, 12 ranked battles, I had enough dark elixer to upgrade 1.5 heros… There are certainly ways to farm a bit faster, but even still, there are 6 heros to upgrade, and would take at least an hour of efficient farming to fill a storage which would maybe be enough to upgrade 3. Upgrades for heros aren’t shorter than any other defense really, taking 4ish days per upgrade at my level, with AT LEAST 10 levels to get through per hero at each town hall, and if you fall behind at all, good luck. To make it worse, while upgrading you can’t use your hero’s, so no war, no ranked, no efficient farming, no practicing strategies, nothing to do, and can’t even work on resources to prepare for the next round of upgrades. If you want to play ranked weekly and keep up with your clan mates, you can’t even keep them continuously upgrading! You have to make sure they are all ready to go for ranked day. As I try to push to level 90 on my hero’s, my enthusiasm to play is utterly killed. The weirdest part is that there is absolutely no one who disagrees that this is the worst part of the game, probably causes more players to quit than anything else, and they have done nothing significant to address it. If we have to get through 41,600 hours of hero upgrades, yes, you heard that right, we should at least not lose the ability to use the hero’s during that time! Common sense.

author: Zemroda
title: Massive Improvements Over Time / Heroes Upgrades are Painful
content:
I had not played this game in several years, predominately due to the troop “training” system, in which troops need to take time (sometimes upwards of 45 minutes or more for a *single* troop). Meanwhile, troops used in battle, even ones that survived the whole thing, are all lost at the end, which incentivized you to use a little troops as possible to invade a base, and made attacking a “nickle and dining” affair raid than an intense, all-out assault that truly demonstrated how powerful your army could be (you didn’t go “all-out” as often as you should). Games like Supercell’s Boom Beach were preferable at this time due to the ability for surviving troops to come back, which incentivized a different type of skill in the form of using all your troops but doing your best to keep them alive.

Fast forward to now, and attacking is entirely free with troops being restored instantly. This has made the game far more engaging in terms of mixing and matching army compositions, attacking constantly to perfect a strategy, and sometimes just attacking for fun. Due to the daily reward of collecting 5 stars from battles (of which 1-3 stars can be earned per battle), you have a daily goal of battles that you can optionally perform and then feel finished once the reward is earned.

The game has had several QoL additions, such as the base build layout manager allowing to easily edit or copy your own base, or copy those of others, as well as having a section for war bases. Assistants now help with various base tasks, and generally speed up the processes. The builder base and clan capital wars give even more to do.

Overall, the game feels much more fun and consumer friendly, with Hero skins and gems (which you can slowly earn for free) being the main purchase options, both of which feel fine.

The only issue I’ve now noticed is the hero upgrade system, as mentioned in the title. Heroes will be in the 10s to 100s of levels (level 150 max from what I know), however, each individual level must be upgraded one at a time, requiring resources like troop training. However, these upgrades can take up to 2 days and beyond for just one upgrade (say a Barbarian King going from level 30 to level 31), AND they use up one of your builders for some reason. Town Hall upgrades usually raise your heroe’s max level cap by another 20 levels (level 30 max to level 50 max, for example), and when you have 3 to 4 heroes (6 max), this can mean a literal month or more of just pure hero upgrades before you can feel as though you’ve completed all upgrades before the next town hall level. Meanwhile, these hero upgrades are slowing down your base upgrades due to using up your builders. On top of all of this, your heroes can’t be used for the upwards of 2 or more days while they’re upgrading, making the entire process painful, hindering, and generally not fun.

Supercell had an event where heroes could be upgrading and still usable (though a builder was used), which was more enjoyable. I personally feel as though the resource requirement (which is currently one of the only good uses for dark exilir with the high dark exilir hero upgrades costs) is a good enough cost, and that allowing heroes to be upgraded while still being usable and NOT using up a builder would be far more enjoyable. Make this change, and the game would be feeling near perfect for what it is trying to offer.

author: PohCacs
title: Nostalgia Mode: Relive Previous Town Halls
content:
I have an idea that I think would make the game even more enjoyable 
Once you upgrade your Town Hall, there’s is not way to go back and experience Older Town Hall levels again. Every Yown Hall has its own unique strategies, troops , and memories, and many players feel nostalgic about them 
It would be great to add a “Nostagial Mode” where players can temporarily choose any previous Town hall level they have already unlocked, For example, if I’m Town Hall 15, I could switch into a practice version of Town Hall 9, 10, or any lower level I have already completed 

I this mode, players could:

•Build their own base layouts for that Town Hall level.

• Attack their own base layouts to practice.

•Try official practice bases provided by the game.

•Use the troops, heroes, and strategies that were available at that Town Hall level.

To keep the game balanced, this mode should not given loot, trophies, ores, or any other rewards. it would be purely for fun, practice, and nostalgia.

I think many long-time players would love the opportunity to revisit older Town Halls and relive the experience while also 
helping newer players practice strategies in a fun way.
